name: 2¾″ Kuruvi
description: The smallest single-report cracker we make and the one that starts most children off. A crisp, dry crack rather than a chest-thump, sold by the box so a strip of them can be lit one after another down a driveway.
highlights: Lightest report in the one-sound range

name: 3½″ Lakshmi
description: The classic Lakshmi in its 3½ inch size — the everyday festival cracker of Tamil Nadu. Tight-rolled paper casing, clean single report, and no smouldering remains to clear up afterwards.

name: 4″ Lakshmi
description: A full inch more casing than the 3½, and it tells. The 4 inch Lakshmi is the size most families settle on once they have tried both — noticeably deeper without moving into deluxe pricing.

name: 4″ Lakshmi Deluxe
description: The deluxe grade of our 4 inch Lakshmi: same size, heavier charge, and a harder paper wrap that holds the pressure longer before it lets go. That extra fraction of a second is the whole difference.
highlights: Reinforced wrap for a sharper report

name: 4″ Gold Lakshmi
description: Our top Lakshmi. Gold-foiled casing, the heaviest charge the 4 inch format takes, and the one we put out for the first light of the morning.
highlights: Heaviest 4 inch charge in the range

name: 5″ Bahubali
description: Five inches of casing and a report you feel before you hear. Bahubali is for open ground only — a courtyard is not enough space for it.
highlights: 5 inch casing, the largest single sound we sell

name: Ola Vedi
description: The old Sivakasi ola vedi, still made the way it always was — palm-leaf wrapped and hand-tied in a long chain. Nothing modern sounds quite like it, which is exactly why it is still in the list.
highlights: Hand-tied chain, lit from one end

name: 28 Chorsa
description: A 28-sound chorsa chain — the short garland, tied flat so it can be laid along a wall or a step rather than hung. Runs through all 28 in about 7 seconds.
highlights: Ties flat — lay it along a wall

name: 56 Chorsa
description: A 56-sound chorsa chain — the short garland, tied flat so it can be laid along a wall or a step rather than hung. Runs through all 56 in about 14 seconds.
highlights: Ties flat — lay it along a wall

name: 28 Giant
description: The giant grade of the 28 chain: same count, heavier charge on every cracker, so it lands harder and carries further across open ground.
highlights: 28 sounds, heavier charge than the Chorsa

name: 56 Giant
description: The giant grade of the 56 chain: same count, heavier charge on every cracker, so it lands harder and carries further across open ground.
highlights: 56 sounds, heavier charge than the Chorsa

name: 24 Deluxe

highlights: Fuller report than the standard garland
Even rhythm from first to last

name: 50 Bijili
description: Fifty small paper crackers loose in a pack. The Bijili is the cracker children are handed first — a light snap, no flame to speak of, and enough of them in a bag to last the whole evening.

name: 100 Bijili
description: The hundred-count Bijili pack — the same small paper cracker, bought the way most families actually buy it. Works out cheaper per cracker than the fifty.
highlights: Better value per cracker than the 50

name: Baby Bullet
description: The entry point of the bullet series. Compact casing, sharp report, and the least intimidating of the four to light.

name: Mini Bullet
description: A step up from the Baby Bullet with a noticeably fuller sound. The size most people buy when they want a bomb but not the biggest one on the shelf.
highlights: Fuller report than the Baby Bullet

name: Mega Bullet
description: The largest of the bullets. Heavy casing, deep report, and a 10 metre safe distance we mean literally.

name: Atom Bomb
description: The atom bomb needs no introduction in Sivakasi. Flat, hard report with no ring to it — the sound everyone pictures when they think of Diwali.
highlights: Flat, hard sound with no ring

name: Hydro Bomb
description: Built around a denser charge than the atom bomb, so the report carries further across open ground. One of the loudest items we are permitted to sell.
highlights: Carries further than the atom bomb

name: King of Kings Bomb
description: The King of Kings sits at the top of the standard bomb range. Reinforced casing, long fuse, and a report that will set off car alarms two streets over.
highlights: Long fuse for a safe retreat
Top of the standard bomb range

name: Classic Bomb
description: Our own house bomb, unchanged since the nineties. If you grew up on Gopi crackers, this is the one you remember.

name: Digital Red & Green Bomb
description: A bomb with a light show attached — a red flash and a green flash a beat apart, then the report. The most-photographed item in the bomb range.
highlights: Red and green flash before the report
The showpiece of the bomb range

name: ¼ kg Paper Bomb
description: A quarter kilo of paper bomb, tied the traditional nattu vedi way. Lit at ground level in open space, well away from walls that would reflect the blast.

name: ½ kg Paper Bomb
description: Half a kilo, and the size most temple and village functions actually order. Hand-tied with a long jute fuse.
images: GOPI Crackers/PAPER BOMB/½ kg Paper Bomb.jfif

name: 1 kg Paper Bomb
description: A full kilo paper bomb — the largest nattu vedi we make, and one that needs a licensed hand and genuinely open ground.
highlights: One kilo charge, the largest we make

GOPI Crackers/PAPER BOMB/½ kg Paper Bomb.jfif

name: Money Bank
description: The money bank is a paper bomb with a party trick: the casing bursts into a shower of printed notes. Loud, then briefly ridiculous.
highlights: Bursts into a shower of printed notes

name: Ground Chakkar Big
description: The standard ground chakkar, twenty-five to a pack. Balanced hub, even spin, and a bright gold disc that holds its shape for the full burn.
highlights: Balanced hub for a wobble-free spin
images: GOPI Crackers/AMAZING GROUND CHAKKARAM/Ground Chakkaram Big.jfif

name: Ground Chakkar Special
description: A heavier charge on the same chassis as the Big. Spins longer and throws a wider disc, with a colour change about two-thirds through.
images: GOPI Crackers/AMAZING GROUND CHAKKARAM/Ground Chakkaram Special.jfif

name: Ground Chakkar Ashoka
description: The Ashoka grade runs close to forty seconds and steps through three colours as it goes. The one to lay out in a row when you want the ground covered.
highlights: Lays out well in a row
images: GOPI Crackers/AMAZING GROUND CHAKKARAM/Ground Chakkaram Special.jfif
GOPI Crackers/AMAZING GROUND CHAKKARAM/Ground Chakkaram Big.jfif

name: Ground Chakkar Deluxe
description: Our deluxe chakkar: double-wound composition, a machined hub, and the longest, flattest spin in the range. It stays put instead of wandering across the floor.

images: GOPI Crackers/AMAZING GROUND CHAKKARAM/Ground Chakkaram Deluxe.jfif

name: Spinner Chakkar Special
description: The spinner leaves the ground. It winds up flat, lifts about a metre, and holds there spinning before it settles back down.
highlights: Lifts about a metre off the ground
Spins in the air before settling

name: Spinner Chakkar Deluxe
description: The deluxe spinner climbs higher and holds longer than the special, with a colour change at the top of the lift. Needs clear sky above — no awnings, no branches.

images: GOPI Crackers/AMAZING GROUND CHAKKARAM/4 x 4 Wheel.jfif

name: Wire Chakkar Special
description: A wire-frame chakkar rather than a paper one, so it spins truer and lasts longer. Ten to a pack, and they can be nailed to a post to spin vertically.

Can be mounted on a post
images: GOPI Crackers/AMAZING GROUND CHAKKARAM/Wire Chakkar (10 Pcs).jfif

name: Wire Chakkar Deluxe
description: The deluxe wire chakkar, with a heavier composition on the same true-running frame. The longest burn of any ground item we sell.

highlights: About a metre of gold fountain

name: Flower Pot Special
description: A wider throat than the Big, so the column opens out rather than going straight up. Brighter and broader for the same burn time.

name: Flower Pot Ashoka
description: The Ashoka pot layers three compositions on top of each other — gold, then green, then crackling silver — so it changes character twice as it burns down.
highlights: Gold to green to crackling silver

name: Flower Pot Deluxe
description: Five deluxe pots to a pack, each running close to a minute. Set them out in an arc and light the middle one first — the spread reads better than a straight line.

name: Flower Pot Super Deluxe
description: Two super deluxe pots, taller and heavier than the standard deluxe, throwing a column near two metres. The pair is sized for a front doorway.

name: Dazzling Pot Deluxe
description: The dazzling pot puts a crackling silver crown on top of a gold column. Loud enough to notice, bright enough to light a whole courtyard.

name: Colour Koti
description: Colour Koti runs through the full colour set — red, green, blue, violet — one after another out of a single pot, with no gold at all.
images: GOPI Crackers/FLOWER POTS/Flower Pots Colour Kotti.jfif

name: Colour Koti Deluxe
description: The deluxe Koti holds each colour longer and adds a fifth stage. The most colour you can get out of one ground item.
highlights: The most colourful pot we make
images: GOPI Crackers/FLOWER POTS/Flower Pots Colour Kotti.jfif

name: Tri Colour Pot
description: Three pots, three colours — saffron, white and green, lit together. Popular for Independence Day as much as for Diwali.

name: Colourful Crackling Pot
description: Five pots of crackling colour. Each one throws a column that snaps and pops the whole way up rather than running silent.

name: Ganga Jamuna
description: Ganga Jamuna runs two compositions side by side out of one pot — a gold column and a silver one, twisting around each other. Named for the two rivers, and it looks it.

name: Soda Fountain
description: Three tall tin fountains that run close to ninety seconds each — the longest burn of any pot in the list. Best lit one at a time so the show lasts.

name: Crackling Fountain Rolls Royce
description: Three fountains of dense crackling silver, thick enough that the column reads as solid from a distance. The most expensive-looking thing on the ground.
highlights: Reads as solid from a distance

name: Monster Pot Super Deluxe
description: The largest pot we make. A single fountain running well over two metres for a minute and a half, changing through four compositions on the way. Give it space and let it be the finale.

name: Helicopter
description: A small ground item that lifts on a paper rotor, climbs three or four metres and comes back down spinning. No report at any stage.

name: Bumbaram
description: The bumbaram spins flat on the ground and hums as it goes — the sound is the point. Old-fashioned and still one of the first things children ask for.

name: Butterfly
description: Paper wings on a small rotor, lit at the base. It flutters rather than flies, in colour, about waist height. Genuinely silent.

name: Small Gun
description: A moulded plastic cap gun sized for small hands, sold with a roll of caps. Reusable season after season.
highlights: Comes with one roll of caps

name: Big Gun
description: The full-size cap gun, heavier in the hand with a louder action and a longer cap roll. The one older children want.

name: Ring Cap
description: Replacement ring caps for either gun. Cheapest item in the catalogue and the one that runs out first — buy more than you think you need.
highlights: Fits both the Small and Big Gun
The item that always runs out first

name: Small Peacock
description: A fountain that opens into a fanned peacock tail of green and gold, about a metre wide. New for 2026 and already one of the most asked-for.

name: Bada Peacock
description: The large peacock — twice the fan of the small one, with a blue stage the small version does not have. Give it two metres of clear ground.
highlights: Twice the fan of the Small Peacock

name: Pappu Shower
description: A soft, wide shower rather than a column — it throws low and broad, which reads beautifully on camera and keeps the sparks well away from anybody watching.
highlights: Sparks stay low to the ground

name: Barlie
description: Four pink and silver fountains, deliberately pretty rather than loud. Sold as a set because they are meant to be lit together.

name: Mega Siren
description: Three sirens that climb in pitch as they spin, then cut out together. More noise than fire — there is barely any flame on this one.

name: Photo Flash
description: Five flash units that fire a hard white burst about a second apart — bright enough to freeze a photograph, which is the whole idea.
highlights: Bright enough to light a photograph

name: Selfie Stick
description: A hand-held fountain on a stick, sized and balanced to hold out at arm's length while somebody takes the picture. Cold-glow composition throughout.

name: Colour Smoke
description: Coloured smoke rather than fire — a dense plume that hangs for a minute or two. Daytime item, and by far the best thing in the list for photographs.
highlights: Daytime item — coloured smoke, no flame
Plume hangs for a minute or two
images: GOPI Crackers/SPECIAL COLLECTION/Colour Smoke Multi Colour.jfif

name: Peacock Feather
description: Five slim fountains that open into overlapping feathers of green and blue. Quieter and more delicate than the Peacock pots.

name: Emu Egg
description: An egg-shaped ground item that cracks open partway through the burn and switches from gold to crackling silver. Odd, and very effective.

name: Panda
description: A small novelty fountain in a printed panda casing — low, gentle and short. Made for the youngest children in the family.

name: Robo Kids
description: A ground novelty that walks a few inches as it burns, throwing sparks from the base. Cheap enough to buy a handful.

name: Tin Single
description: A single tin fountain, tall and stable, that runs a clean gold column for about a minute. The simplest thing in the 2026 list and one of the best-judged.
highlights: Clean gold column, about a minute

name: Magic Paper Pop Pop
description: Paper pop-pops thrown at the ground. No flame, no fuse, nothing to light — the only item here you can hand to a child unsupervised.
highlights: No flame and nothing to light

name: Miracle Pots
description: A small pot that changes colour three times in a very short burn. Sold cheap so you can put a dozen out at once, which is how it looks best.
highlights: Three colours in a short burn
Meant to be lit a dozen at a time

name: Star Drum
description: A drum-shaped fountain that throws a ring of sparks rather than a column, with a star-shaped spread at the top of the burn.
highlights: Throws a ring, not a column

name: Water Queen
description: The water queen runs a rippling blue-white fountain that looks closer to water than fire. Silent, and the gentlest thing in the 2026 list.
highlights: The gentlest item in the 2026 range

name: Maha Asrafi
description: The large asrafi: a dense gold fountain in a squat casing, built to look like a bar of gold and to burn like one. Heavier charge than the standard Asrafi.

name: Asrafi
description: The standard asrafi — the same gold-bar casing and composition in a smaller size. Steady, bright and hard to get wrong.

name: Kit Kat
description: A flat bar-shaped novelty that snaps in sequence along its length. Small, cheap, and oddly satisfying.
highlights: Snaps in sequence along the bar

name: Bat Ball
description: A cricket-bat-shaped fountain, held or stood on end, that runs a bright silver spray from the shoulder of the bat. A gift item as much as a cracker.
highlights: Works as a gift on its own

name: AK 47 Gun
description: A rifle-shaped fountain that fires a long, flat spray from the muzzle. Stood on its stock and lit — never held, despite the shape.
highlights: Long flat spray from the muzzle
Stand it on the stock — never hold it

name: Top Gun
description: The heavier of the two gun fountains, with a longer barrel and a two-stage burn that finishes on crackling silver.
highlights: Stand and light — do not hold

name: Appu Fountain
description: An elephant-shaped fountain that throws from the trunk. Children pick this one off the shelf before they read anything about it.

name: Ice Cone
description: A cone fountain that throws a soft, rounded spray rather than a hard column — closer to a shaving of light than a jet.

name: Kulfi
description: Named for the ice cream, and it does look like one: a tall, narrow fountain in a printed casing that runs cream-white then breaks into colour.

name: King Version Fountain
description: A large fountain built around a heavy central charge, so the column holds its height for the whole burn instead of tailing off.
highlights: Holds its height for the full burn

name: Smoke Bomb Cylinder
description: Two smoke cylinders that put out a thick, low-lying cloud for well over a minute each. Daytime item, and the best value in the smoke range.
highlights: Over a minute each, pack of 2

name: 90's Kids
description: A mixed pack of the small novelties that were everywhere in the nineties — snaps, pencils, colour crush and a few pop-pops. Sold on nostalgia, and it works.
